title: What's new in v2.8.0
summary: Network Optimizer can read Wi-Fi data from the access points themselves now, which means live client data twice a second, a client that stays followed across a roam, a way to move one where you want it, and per-client LAN throughput the Console never counted.

steps.title: AP Telemetry
steps.listLabel: Read Wi-Fi data straight from your access points
steps.body: Read Wi-Fi data from the access points themselves instead of only from the UniFi Console: faster live client data, per-client LAN throughput, roam records, and radio health. Switch it on and a small ephemeral agent is pushed to each access point over SSH.

steps.title: Client Performance
steps.listLabel: Live client data twice a second, and it keeps up through a roam
steps.body: With **AP Telemetry** on, this page reads the client's own access point twice a second. Signal, PHY rates, and throughput move as fast as the client does, and when it roams the page follows it to the new access point instead of stalling on the handoff.

steps.title: Roam
steps.listLabel: Move a client to a better band or access point
steps.body: **Roam** asks a client to move: **Change Band** to push it up to a faster band it has used before, or **Change AP** to hand it to a neighbor. Useful on a walk test, when you need the device on the access point you are testing rather than wherever it is clinging. Network Optimizer sends a short, targeted candidate list, because a long one gets ignored.

steps.title: Live View
steps.listLabel: See LAN traffic your Console never counted
steps.body: UniFi Network counts what crossed the gateway, so a client copying to a NAS, streaming from your media server, or running a LAN speed test read as idle no matter how hard the link was working. Reading the counters on the access point measures what is actually on the air, so that traffic shows up per client for the first time.
